title: Introduce conditional RBAC roles for cross-region service operators, KMS routing assertions, and audit redactors
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds conditional RBAC roles scoped to service+region, propagates KMS routing assertions into request metadata, and implements server-side audit redaction rules. Includes migration script and feature flag rollout.
description:
Context and motivation: Customers operating across multiple cloud regions asked for a way to grant operators limited admin capabilities that are scoped both by service and by region, and for KMS usage to be auditable without expanding global key access. This PR introduces a conditional RBAC role model (RBAC v2 predicate-based roles) that can express 'service X in region Y' constraints, adds KMS routing assertions that follow requests through the stack, and a pluggable server-side audit redactor to strip sensitive fields from logs for regulated tenants.

What changed (summary):
- New predicate-based RBAC conditions and enforcement in the policy engine; policies can include attributes: region, service, task (read/write), and temporal windows.
- Middleware to derive and propagate a signed KMS-routing assertion header (x-rw-kms-assertion) populated from the request's tenancy + region preference.
- Audit redactor component that consults tenant compliance profile and redacts or hashes configured fields before persisting to the audit store. Redaction rules are configurable via the security-config map.
- Migration script and feature flag (security.conditional_rbac) to allow gradual rollout and rollback.
- Unit and integration tests plus a small performance sanity suite demonstrating <0.7ms median add-on latency for the new middleware when enabled.

Checklist: [x] policy model defined and documented; [x] enforcement integrated into request pipeline; [x] migration script added; [x] tests covering policy evaluation and KMS header correctness; [x] docs updated; [x] feature-flag gated rollout.

Small illustrative snippet (policy syntax example):
policy allow-operator-region {
  subject: role:service-operator
  resource: service:storage-queue
  action: write
  condition: region == "eu-west-1" && hour >= 08 && hour <= 18
}

CI and validation:
- CI run 1 (initial): lint passed, unit tests failed (flake in policy loader test) -> author reworked loader and added stabilizing test harness.
- CI run 2: all unit tests passed, integration suite passed in GHA fanned runners, security static analysis reported 1 minor issue (unused var) fixed.
- Performance: micro-bench for middleware shows ~0.5–0.7ms median extra cost when the feature flag is on; disabled by default so host impact is zero until rollout.

Migration and rollout notes:
- Migration script creates new policy attribute indexes and a small set of default service-scoped operator roles. The feature is gated behind security.conditional_rbac; we recommend enabling for a single region and observing metrics for 48h before full rollout.
- Rollback: disabling feature flag returns policy evaluation to prior behavior; migration script is reversible but requires manual cleanup when removing indexes.

Security considerations:
- KMS routing assertions are signed using the service signing key; verification is required in downstream services before any key use.
- Audit redactor cannot be used to hide system-level security events; the redactor runs only on tenant-level event payloads, and system events are preserved.

Merge outcome: Squash merged into main by Arjun Patel. No follow-up blockers noted.
